name: com.taalhammer/taalhammer
title: Taalhammer
description: Learn languages in Claude: review your flashcards, track progress, build collections, ask questions.

tools.name: search_articles
tools.description: When the user asks what Taalhammer says or recommends about learning a language — e.g. "according to Taalhammer, how many new words a day?", "zgodnie z metodyką Taalhammera…" — methods and research (spaced repetition, sleep, listening, grammar, motivation), how a Taalhammer feature works, how it compares with other apps, or grammar and vocabulary of a language Taalhammer writes about. Returns passages from Taalhammer's own published articles, each with its title and a link to www.taalhammer.com, plus fixed facts about the app (features, availability, no offline mode), so an answer can cite the source. Plans and prices are get_plans_and_prices. Read-only; no account needed.

query.description: Search phrase IN ENGLISH (translated from the user's language when they write in another one). A few keywords or one question, e.g. 'does sleep help vocabulary learning', 'how does Drill mode work', 'de or het Dutch articles'.

user_language.description: ISO code of the language the user writes in, e.g. 'pl' or 'en'. 'pl' returns passages from Polish articles where they exist; any other value returns English articles.

topic.description: What the question is about: 'methodology' (how to learn, the research — e.g. spaced repetition, sleep), 'app' (a Taalhammer feature, account or how-to — e.g. Listen mode), 'comparison' (Taalhammer vs other apps or methods), 'language' (grammar or vocabulary of one language — set `language`).

language.description: Optional ISO code or name of the language being learned, e.g. 'nl', 'de'. Taalhammer has grammar and vocabulary articles about English, German, Dutch and Italian, and a few course, alphabet or pronunciation pages about Greek, Norwegian, Korean, Chinese, Japanese and Arabic. For other languages the result says that no article is specifically about it.

tools.name: get_radio_stations
tools.description:
When the user wants to listen to radio in the language they are learning — e.g.
"which German radio stations can I listen to?", "is there Dutch radio in
Taalhammer?". Returns the live stations Taalhammer curates per language, each with
a link to the station's own website, where it can be listened to, and a short
description. language='all': the languages that have stations, with how many each.
Without a language: signed in, the stations of the main language the user learns
(plus the other languages' counts); otherwise the language list.
Real stations, not generated audio. Read-only; no account needed.

language.description: Optional language name or ISO code, e.g. 'German' or 'de'. 'all' = the languages that have stations, with how many each. Empty = the main language the user learns when signed in, otherwise the same list as 'all'.

tools.name: get_plans_and_prices
tools.description: When the user asks what Taalhammer costs or which plans it has — e.g. "how much does Taalhammer cost?", "is there a lifetime plan?", "ile kosztuje Taalhammer?". Returns the plans and prices published on taalhammer.com's pricing page (EUR; PLN on the Polish page), with the page's link. Prices in the App Store and Google Play can differ. The user's own plan is get_my_subscription_status. Read-only; no account needed.

user_language.description: ISO code of the language the user writes in, e.g. 'en', 'pl', 'de'. 'pl' returns the Polish pricing page (PLN), 'de' the German one; any other value the English page (EUR).

tools.name: search_catalog
tools.description:
When the user is choosing what to learn and asks whether they can learn a
language with Taalhammer or whether a ready-made course exists — e.g. "can I learn
Japanese with Taalhammer?", "is there a French course for Spanish speakers?".
Returns
Taalhammer's official language-learning catalog for a language pair: Core courses
by CEFR level and themed Topic packs, saying what exists and what does not. Unlike
search_collections, it needs no account and covers only Taalhammer's own courses,
not the user's own collections. With no arguments: an overview of the language pairs.
A pair without a ready-made course can still be learned with the user's own
collections (about 75 languages).

source.description: Language the user already speaks, name or ISO code, e.g. 'Polish' or 'pl'.

target.description: Language the user wants to learn, e.g. 'English' or 'en'.

kind.description: 'core' (the graded A1–C2 courses), 'topic' (themed packs) or empty for both.

query.description: Topic to find in titles, e.g. 'cooking'.

level.description: CEFR level filter for topics, e.g. 'B1'.

tools.name: get_my_stats
tools.description:
When the user asks about their learning progress or statistics — e.g. "show me
my learning progress", "how many words have I learned?", "how many reviews do I
have today?", "what's my streak?". Returns the user's own Taalhammer overview:
reviews due today and tomorrow, words learned, active language(s), study
streak, today's activity, then the review forecast
for the next 7 days as a table (and a bar chart image). Read-only; requires
the user's Taalhammer account.

chart.description: Also return the forecast as a bar-chart image, e.g. true (default) or false for text only.

language.description: Optional language being learned, name or ISO code, e.g. 'Dutch' or 'nl'. Empty = all the user's active languages.

tools.name: get_memory_curve
tools.description:
When the user asks how much of what they learned they will remember or forget —
e.g. "how many of my words will I forget?", "show my forgetting curve", "how well
do I remember my cards?". Returns the user's own Taalhammer memory estimate from
the FSRS scheduler: cards safe, at risk and likely forgotten today, and the expected
recall over the next 30 days without reviews, as a table (and a line chart image).
Available for accounts on the FSRS scheduler; for others the result says so.
Read-only; requires the user's Taalhammer account.

chart.description: Also return the curve as a line-chart image, e.g. true (default) or false for text only.

language.description: Optional language being learned, name or ISO code, e.g. 'Dutch' or 'nl'. Empty = all the user's languages.

tools.name: get_weakest_cards
tools.description:
When the user asks which words or cards they struggle with — e.g. "which words
do I keep forgetting?", "what are my weakest cards?", "what should I practise
more?". Returns the user's hardest flashcards from their own Taalhammer
reviews: cards rated Difficult in the last 30 days or with the lowest memory
stability, each with both sides, the reason, times failed and its collection.
Read-only. Practising them is get_review_cards with type 'drill'. Requires the
user's Taalhammer account.

langs.description: Optional language(s) being learned, comma-separated ISO codes, e.g. 'nl'.

tools.name: get_my_content_subscriptions
tools.description:
When the user asks which collections or decks they have — e.g. "what's in my
library?", "which collections am I subscribed to?". Returns the user's
Taalhammer collections (their own and those added from the library) with
language pair, card counter and id, followed by what can be studied
now: Favourites, each collection and the scheduled reviews due. This is the
content library; the paid plan is get_my_subscription_status. Requires the
user's Taalhammer account.

tools.name: get_my_subscription_status
tools.description:
When the user asks about their Taalhammer plan or billing — e.g. "what plan
am I on?", "when does my trial end?", "did my subscription expire?". Returns
the user's access type, trial state, expiry date and where the subscription
is billed (web, App Store or Google Play). The user's collections are
get_my_content_subscriptions. Requires the user's Taalhammer account.

tools.name: get_review_cards
tools.description:
When the user wants a review session — to study, practise, do their reviews
or be quizzed on their flashcards — e.g. "let's do my Taalhammer review
session", "quiz me on my Dutch collection". Starts a study round from the
user's account: reviews due now, new or hard cards, one collection, or
Favourites. Returns each card's id, prompt and answer language, not the
answer. Taalhammer cards are studied by self-assessment: the learner recalls
the answer, sees it (get_card_answer), then rates it Easy / Almost / Difficult
(grade 5 / 3 / 1); grade_card records the rating. Side effect: the cards
are marked as pulled and count toward the free plan's daily card allowance
(get_collection reads cards without that).

size.description: How many cards to fetch, 1–20, e.g. 5.

type.description: 'scheduled' (reviews due now), 'new' (cards never seen), 'drill' (hard cards again, e.g. the weakest ones), 'learn' (first learning of one collection or Favourites).

collection_id.description: Optional id of one collection, from get_my_content_subscriptions or search_collections, e.g. '12345'. Empty = Favourites (all active collections mixed).

tools.name: grade_card
tools.description:
When the user rates how well they recalled a card from get_review_cards —
e.g. "easy", "I almost had it", "no idea". Records the self-assessment on the
user's Taalhammer account and returns that card's answer, its next review
date and the prompt of the next card in the batch. Taalhammer cards are
studied by self-assessment: the learner recalls the answer, sees it
(get_card_answer), then rates it Easy / Almost / Difficult (grade 5 / 3 / 1);
a card is rated once per round. Taalhammer's spaced-repetition
algorithm schedules the next review from the rating. Requires the user's
account.

smid.description: The card's id from get_review_cards, e.g. '27478'.

grade.description: The learner's rating: 1 = Difficult (not recalled), 3 = Almost (recalled with effort), 5 = Easy (recalled at once).

tools.name: get_card_answer
tools.description:
When the user has tried to recall a card from get_review_cards — typed
their answer, or asks to see it — or taps "Show answer" in the Taalhammer card
view. Returns the answer side of that card and whether it was already rated in
this round. Taalhammer cards are studied by self-assessment, in this order: the
learner recalls, sees the answer, then rates the card Easy / Almost / Difficult
(grade_card). Read-only; requires the user's Taalhammer account.

smid.description: The card's id from get_review_cards, e.g. '27478'.

tools.name: create_collection
tools.description:
When the user wants an empty collection with a given name — e.g. "create a new
collection called 'Kitchen words'", "save them to a new collection called
'Love'". A new collection with cards written on a topic is make_collection
(a form). Creates an empty named
collection in the user's account and returns its id; cards are then added with
import_flashcards (up to 200 per call) or in the app's Creator. The collection is
private: only the user sees it. Requires the user's Taalhammer account.

title.description: Collection title, e.g. 'Dutch kitchen words — A2'.

source.description: ISO code of the language the user knows, e.g. 'en'.

target.description: ISO code of the language being learned, e.g. 'nl'.

description.description: Optional short description shown in the app, e.g. 'Words for cooking at home'.

even_if_just_saved.description: True (e.g. true) = create it even though the cards of the latest preview for this language pair were saved in the last 10 minutes.

tools.name: import_flashcards
tools.description:
When the user wants cards saved to a collection they have named or chosen —
e.g. "add these sentences to my 'Kitchen words' collection", "save them to the
new one". Adds the given card texts (a
word, phrase or sentence with a source side and a target side) to one of the
user's collections, where they enter the user's spaced-repetition reviews. Text
only: this tool creates no audio or images; the app voices a card when it is
played. At most 200 cards per call, each side up to 2,000 characters; the
collection must exist and belong to the user (create_collection makes one).
Requires the user's Taalhammer account.

collection_id.description: Id of the user's own collection, from create_collection or get_my_content_subscriptions, e.g. '12345'.

source_lang.description: ISO code of the source side, e.g. 'en'.

target_lang.description: ISO code of the target side, e.g. 'nl'.

tools.name: preview_flashcards
tools.description:
When the user wants flashcards written in the conversation saved and has not
named the collection they go to — e.g. "save these words", "show me the cards
first" — or once the cards of a new collection are written. Lists the card texts with where they can go: one of the user's own
collections for that language pair, or a new collection with a name. In the
Taalhammer card view the user picks the collection and saves there. Checked
against the same limits as saving (1–200 cards, each side up to 2,000
characters). Saves nothing itself; saving is import_flashcards (create_collection
for a new one). Requires the user's Taalhammer account.

source_lang.description: ISO code of the source side, e.g. 'en'.

target_lang.description: ISO code of the target side, e.g. 'nl'.

collection_id.description: Optional id of the user's own collection the cards would go to, e.g. '12345'. Empty = the user's own collection for this language pair that new cards go to first.

new_title.description: Optional name for a NEW collection, e.g. 'Love — Dutch A2'. Given without collection_id = the cards are offered for a new collection with this name.

level.description: Optional CEFR level of the cards, e.g. 'A2' (A1–C2); a new collection is created with it.

tools.name: make_collection
tools.description:
When the user wants a new Taalhammer collection, deck or set of flashcards made,
created or written for them on a topic — e.g. "make me a Taalhammer collection
about love", "create a Dutch deck about food", "make flashcards about travelling".
Opens a form to make the new collection: topic, language pair, CEFR level and
number of cards, filled from the request and the user's account. Writes and saves
no cards; the values the user confirms in the form are returned by
get_collection_settings. The result lists Taalhammer's rules for course cards.
Requires the user's Taalhammer account.

topic.description: What the cards are about, e.g. 'love' or 'at the doctor'.

source_language.description: Language the learner already speaks, name or ISO code, e.g. 'Polish' or 'pl'. Empty = the account's native language.

target_language.description: Language being learned, e.g. 'Dutch' or 'nl'. Empty = the account's main language.

tools.name: get_collection_settings
tools.description:
When the user has confirmed the Taalhammer new-collection form from make_collection
— e.g. says "go", "ok" or "write them" after clicking “Use these settings”. Returns
the values confirmed in the form: number of cards, language pair, CEFR level, topic
and the suggested name for a new collection. Read-only; requires the user's
Taalhammer account.

tools.name: collection_request_text
tools.description:
When the user clicks "Write the cards" in the Taalhammer new-collection form.
Returns the confirmed choice as facts and keeps it for get_collection_settings; the
form also hands it to Claude as context for the user's next message. Called by the form
only (MCP Apps visibility "app"). Saves nothing to the account.

tools.name: search_collections
tools.description:
When the user looks for flashcard collections to study in Taalhammer — e.g.
"find me a Dutch B1 collection", "anything about Indonesian food?". Returns
matching collections with title, size, languages and id, from Taalhammer's
library (Core and Topic courses) or from the user's own lists. Unlike
search_catalog, it includes the user's own collections and needs the user's
Taalhammer account; get_collection shows a result's cards.

query.description: Title or topic words, e.g. 'food' or 'B1'. Empty = everything in the filter.

source.description: ISO code of the language the user knows, e.g. 'en'.

target.description: ISO code of the language being learned, e.g. 'nl', 'id' or 'de'.

filter.description: 'public' (Taalhammer's whole library, default), 'core' (Taalhammer Core courses), 'topic' (Taalhammer topic packs), 'trending', 'stream' (the user's subscribed collections), 'user' (collections the user made), 'learned' (collections the user studied before).

tools.name: get_collection
tools.description:
When the user wants to see what is inside a Taalhammer collection — e.g. "what's
in this collection?", "show me the cards of my Dutch deck". Returns the
collection's title, language pair, level, description and a page of its
flashcards (the source and target text of each card). Reading does not mark any
card as studied. Requires the user's Taalhammer account.

collection_id.description: Collection id from search_collections or get_my_content_subscriptions, e.g. '12345'.

start.description: Offset of the first card, e.g. 0 or 50.

tools.name: subscribe_collection
tools.description:
When the user wants to start learning a collection — e.g. "add this collection to
my library". Adds a Taalhammer collection to the user's library for both Learn
(spaced-repetition reviews) and Listen, as "Add to My Library" does in the app; it
then appears in Favourites. Changes the user's account; the id comes from
search_collections or get_collection, an id from elsewhere is not found.

collection_id.description: Collection id from search_collections or get_collection, e.g. '12345'.

tools.name: unsubscribe_collection
tools.description:
When the user wants to stop learning a collection — e.g. "remove this collection
from my library". Removes it from the user's library in both Learn and Listen.
For a collection the user does not own this is permanent: adding it again starts
its progress from zero. Collections the user made stay in their Creator. Changes
the user's account.

collection_id.description: Id of a collection in the user's library, e.g. '12345'.

tools.name: add_to_favourites
tools.description:
When the user wants a collection in their daily study or listening — e.g. "put my
Dutch deck back in my favourites". Puts a collection from the user's library into
Favourites (the heart in the app); Favourites are what Learn and Listen serve, a
collection outside them stays in the library unserved. Changes the user's account.

collection_id.description: Id of a collection already in the user's library, e.g. '12345'.

stream.description: 'learn', 'listen' or 'both' (default) — Learn and Listen Favourites are separate.

tools.name: remove_from_favourites
tools.description:
When the user wants to pause a collection without removing it — e.g. "take this
deck out of my daily reviews". Takes a collection out of Favourites (the heart in
the app): it stays in the library, but Learn and/or Listen no longer serve it.
Reversible with add_to_favourites, progress kept. Changes the user's account.

collection_id.description: Id of a collection in the user's library, e.g. '12345'.

stream.description: 'learn', 'listen' or 'both' (default) — Learn and Listen Favourites are separate.
